title: Loop Engineering For Newbies
subtitle: Designing the system that prompts your agent for you: stop conditions, context budgets, parallel checkouts, and maker-checker splits — explained for newbies
author: BookForge

outline.title: Stop Prompting, Start Looping
outline.summary: The one-prompt-at-a-time era is ending: what 'loop engineering' actually means, the quotes that named it, and the buzzword-bingo around it.

outline.title: The While Loop Under Your Agent
outline.summary: Every coding session is secretly a while loop: assemble context, reason, act, observe, repeat — where the ReAct pattern came from and why coding can't be done in one shot.

outline.title: The Hardest Part Is Knowing When to Stop
outline.summary: Stop conditions as first-class design: what 'done' really means, goal checks versus 'the model stopped talking', iteration caps, timeouts, and spotting an agent spinning in place.

outline.title: The Five Pieces (Plus the Memory)
outline.summary: The building blocks every loop needs — automations, worktrees, skills, connectors, sub-agents — plus the sixth thing that sounds too dumb to matter: a memory file outside the conversation.

outline.title: Give Your Loop a Heartbeat
outline.summary: Making the loop actually run itself: scheduled automations, /loop, /goal, cron, and hooks — plus a real morning-triage loop run against Sentry alerts, and what it takes to trust it running.

outline.title: Two Agents, Two Checkouts
outline.summary: The moment you run two agents, files start colliding: how worktrees keep parallel loops from stepping on each other, what 'isolation' means for context, and why your review bandwidth is the real ceiling.

outline.title: The Agent Forgets. The Repo Doesn't.
outline.summary: State files, AGENTS.md conventions, structured note-taking, and skills — the on-disk memory that keeps a loop smart across runs, because the model forgets everything between sessions.

outline.title: Your Context Window Is a Budget
outline.summary: How context bloats inside a loop: the 888-to-18,900 token growth curve, 'lost in the middle', compaction styles, thrashing, and the real benchmark numbers behind the trade-offs.

outline.title: Keep the Maker Away from the Checker
outline.summary: Why the model that wrote the code is too nice grading its own homework: verifier sub-agents, QA passes at each step, loops that leave evidence behind, and making 'done' mean something.

outline.title: Build the Loop. Stay the Engineer.
outline.summary: The honest fine print: loops that eat tokens, comprehension debt, cognitive surrender, and the human gates some decisions need — where to draw the line, and how to start with one small loop this weekend.
